items.morphologySummary: Triangular soma with apical tuft in Layer 1, basal dendritic skirt, and dense horizontal/associative cortico-cortical axon collaterals.
items.physiologicalRole: Integrates local L4 feedforward and L1 top-down inputs; exhibits regular spiking with Ca2+-activated K+ adaptation.

items.morphologySummary: Large pyramidal soma in Layer 5B with thick apical trunk reaching Layer 1 (Ca2+ spike initiation zone) and long subcortical axon.
items.physiologicalRole: Principal cortical output neuron projecting to spinal cord, brainstem, striatum, and thalamus; supports burst and regular firing.

items.morphologySummary: Compact multipolar star-shaped spiny dendrite arbor lacking a tall apical trunk, confined largely within Layer 4 barrels/columns.
items.physiologicalRole: Primary recipient of core thalamocortical relay axons (VPL, LGN, MGN), amplifying and distributing sensory drive to Layer 2/3.

items.morphologySummary: Deep cortical pyramidal neuron with apical dendrite terminating in Layer 4 and axon projecting back to thalamic relay and TRN nuclei.
items.physiologicalRole: Provides massive modulatory feedback to thalamus and TRN to tune sensory gain and thalamocortical oscillations.

items.morphologySummary: Bipolar-like pyramidal cell with basal dendrites in stratum oriens and stratified apical oblique/tuft dendrites in stratum radiatum and lacunosum-moleculare.
items.physiologicalRole: Integrates CA3 Schaffer collaterals with direct entorhinal Layer 3 inputs; canonical cellular model for NMDA-dependent LTP and place coding.

items.morphologySummary: Large pyramidal neuron bearing proximal thorny excrescences (mossy fiber targets) and extensive longitudinal recurrent collateral axons.
items.physiologicalRole: Drives auto-associative attractor pattern completion and initiates hippocampal sharp-wave ripples.

items.morphologySummary: Compact elliptical soma with cone-shaped spiny dendritic tree in the molecular layer and unmyelinated mossy fiber axon with giant boutons.
items.physiologicalRole: Maintains hyperpolarized resting potential and sparse firing to orthogonalize overlapping entorhinal inputs (pattern separation).

items.morphologySummary: Multipolar aspiny dendrites and dense perisomatic axonal basket terminals enveloping pyramidal cell bodies and proximal dendrites.
items.physiologicalRole: Delivers rapid, powerful perisomatic inhibition; paces 30–80 Hz PING gamma oscillations and enforces narrow coincidence windows.

items.morphologySummary: Distinctive vertical axonal cartridges ('candles') synapsing exclusively onto the Axon Initial Segment (AIS) of pyramidal neurons.
items.physiologicalRole: Directly gates action potential initiation at the AIS across hundreds of neighboring pyramidal cells.

items.morphologySummary: Ascending axon arborizing densely in Layer 1 to contact distal apical dendritic tufts of pyramidal neurons.
items.physiologicalRole: Mediates frequency-dependent facilitating feedback inhibition (via STP facilitation) gating dendritic Ca2+ spikes.

items.morphologySummary: Bipolar vertically oriented interneuron in superficial layers receiving long-range cortical feedback and cholinergic/serotonergic inputs.
items.physiologicalRole: Selectively inhibits SST+ and PV+ interneurons, disinhibiting pyramidal dendrites during active behavior and learning.

items.morphologySummary: Pear-shaped soma with a massive planar fan-shaped dendritic arbor (~150,000 parallel fiber spines) and GABAergic axon to deep cerebellar nuclei.
items.physiologicalRole: Fires intrinsic high-frequency simple spikes (~50 Hz) modulated by climbing-fiber complex spikes to sculpt cerebellar motor output.

items.morphologySummary: Tiny soma (5–8 µm) with 3–5 claw-like dendrites receiving mossy fiber rosettes and an ascending axon bifurcating into parallel fibers.
items.physiologicalRole: Most numerous neuron type in the human brain (~50 billion), performing high-dimensional expansion recoding of sensorimotor context.

items.morphologySummary: Large interneuron in the granular layer with apical dendrites in the molecular layer and dense axonal plexus in cerebellar glomeruli.
items.physiologicalRole: Provides feedforward and feedback GABAergic inhibition onto granule cell dendrites to sharpen mossy-fiber temporal coding.

items.canonicalName: Striatal Direct-Pathway D1 Medium Spiny Neuron (dMSN)
aliases: Striatal Direct-Pathway D1 Medium Spiny Neuron (dMSN)
items.morphologySummary: Medium-sized multipolar soma with densely spiny dendrites expressing Gs-coupled Dopamine D1 receptors, projecting to GPi and SNr.
items.physiologicalRole: Inhibits GPi/SNr output nuclei upon corticostriatal and dopaminergic activation to promote ('Go') selected motor and cognitive actions.

items.canonicalName: Striatal Indirect-Pathway D2 Medium Spiny Neuron (iMSN)
aliases: Striatal Indirect-Pathway D2 Medium Spiny Neuron (iMSN)
items.morphologySummary: Medium-sized spiny projection neuron expressing Gi-coupled Dopamine D2 receptors and enkephalin, projecting selectively to GPe.
items.physiologicalRole: Engages the indirect GPe-STN-GPi pathway to suppress ('No-Go') competing or unrewarded actions; inhibited by dopamine.

items.morphologySummary: Large multipolar ventral horn soma (Lamina IX) with broad dendritic tree and thick myelinated A-alpha axon terminating at neuromuscular junctions.
items.physiologicalRole: Final common motor output unit recruited according to Henneman's size principle to drive extrafusal skeletal muscle fiber contraction.

items.canonicalName: Dorsal Root Ganglion Pseudounipolar Sensory Neuron
aliases: Dorsal Root Ganglion Pseudounipolar Sensory Neuron
items.morphologySummary: Spherical soma in the DRG with a single stem axon bifurcating into a peripheral receptor branch and a central dorsal-root branch.
items.physiologicalRole: Transduces peripheral mechanical (A-beta Piezo2) or nociceptive/thermal (A-delta/C TRPV1/NaV1.7) stimuli without somatic synaptic delay.

items.canonicalName: Retinal Ganglion Cell (M, P & Melanopsin ipRGC)
aliases: Retinal Ganglion Cell (M, P & Melanopsin ipRGC)
items.morphologySummary: Inner retinal output neuron with stratified inner-plexiform dendrites and long optic-nerve axon projecting to LGN, SC, and SCN.
items.physiologicalRole: Encodes ON-center/OFF-surround contrast, motion,chromatic opponency, and ambient circadian irradiance (OPN4 melanopsin).

items.morphologySummary: Bushy radiate dendritic arbor in thalamic relay nuclei expressing prominent low-threshold T-type Ca2+ (CaV3.1) and HCN (Ih) channels.
items.physiologicalRole: Switches between linear tonic single-spike transmission (depolarized wakefulness) and rhythmic low-threshold Ca2+ bursting (hyperpolarized NREM sleep).

items.morphologySummary: Fusiform GABAergic neuron in the reticular shell with dense intranuclear collateral inhibition and projections into dorsal thalamic nuclei.
items.physiologicalRole: Generates sleep spindle oscillations (11–16 Hz) via reciprocal T-current rebound bursts with thalamocortical relay neurons.

items.morphologySummary: Autonomous pacemaker neuron (1–5 Hz tonic firing) with massive unmyelinated axonal arbor forming hundreds of thousands of striatal/cortical varicosities.
items.physiologicalRole: Transitions from tonic pacemaking to phasic bursts (+RPE) or pauses (-RPE) to broadcast reward prediction errors and modulate striatal vigor.

items.morphologySummary: Spongiform bush-like glial cell with thousands of fine perisynaptic leaflets (tripartite synapse) and aquaporin-4 vascular endfeet.
items.physiologicalRole: Buffers extracellular K+ (Kir4.1), clears synaptic glutamate (EAAT1/EAAT2), shuttles lactate, and mediates neurovascular coupling.

items.morphologySummary: Elongated glial cell aligned along myelinated white-matter tracts with long unbranched GFAP-rich processes contacting nodes of Ranvier.
items.physiologicalRole: Supports nodal ionic homeostasis and structural/metabolic integrity along long-range white-matter pathways.

items.morphologySummary: CNS glial cell extending multiple processes to wrap 20–50 axonal internodal segments in compact lipid-rich myelin membranes.
items.physiologicalRole: Reduces internodal capacitance to enable rapid saltatory action potential conduction and supplies axonal lactate via MCT1.

items.morphologySummary: Neural-crest-derived PNS glial cell wrapping a single axonal internode in compact myelin enclosed by a continuous basal lamina.
items.physiologicalRole: Enables rapid peripheral saltatory conduction and forms Bands of Büngner to guide peripheral axonal regeneration after injury.

items.morphologySummary: Yolk-sac-derived resident myeloid cell with highly motile ramified processes continuously scanning the local synaptic microenvironment.
items.physiologicalRole: Executes immune surveillance, phagocytosis of apoptotic debris, and complement-dependent (C1q/C3) developmental synaptic pruning.

items.morphologySummary: Cuboidal/columnar neuroepithelial cell with motile apical kinocilia and microvilli lining the cerebral ventricles and central canal.
items.physiologicalRole: Drives directional near-wall cerebrospinal fluid flow and forms a regulated metabolic interface between CSF and brain parenchyma.

items.morphologySummary: Micrometer-scale actin-rich protrusion (head 0.5–1 µm + narrow neck) housing the PSD-95 scaffold, AMPA/NMDA receptors, and spine apparatus.
items.physiologicalRole: Biochemically and electrically compartmentalizes postsynaptic Ca2+ signals to enable synapse-specific LTP and LTD.

items.canonicalName: Axon Initial Segment (AIS) & Node of Ranvier Compartment
aliases: Axon Initial Segment (AIS) & Node of Ranvier Compartment
items.morphologySummary: Proximal 20–60 µm unmyelinated axonal segment organized by ankyrin-G/beta-IV spectrin clustering high-density NaV1.2/1.6 and Kv7 channels.
items.physiologicalRole: Lowest-threshold trigger zone for action potential initiation and site of homeostatic structural plasticity and chandelier-cell inhibition.
